content: 1. Kasambira TS et al. conducted a study on the use of the QuantiFERON-TB Gold In-Tube test for detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection in children who had household contact with tuberculosis cases. The findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2011, volume 15, issue 5, pages 628–634. 2. Kenyon TA et al. identified risk factors for the transmission of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from HIV-infected tuberculosis patients in Botswana. This study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2002, volume 6, issue 10, pages 843–850. 3. Klausner JD et al. investigated the prevalence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis among household contacts of HIV-1 seropositive patients with active pulmonary tuberculosis in Kinshasa, Zaire. The results were published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 1993, volume 168, issue 1, pages 106–111. 4. Bokhari SY et al. conducted a study on tuberculosis contacts, which was published in the Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association in 1987, volume 37, issue 2, pages 48–52. 5. Biraro IA et al. explored the potential of interferon-gamma-inducible protein 10 as a biomarker for diagnosing latent tuberculosis infection in Uganda. The study was published in PLoS One in 2016, volume 11, issue 1, article e0146098. 6. Rutherford ME et al. compared the QuantiFERON-TB Gold In-Tube assay with the tuberculin skin test in Indonesian children living with a tuberculosis case. The findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2012, volume 16, issue 4, pages 496–502. 7. Tornee S et al. identified risk factors for tuberculosis infection among household contacts in Bangkok, Thailand. The study was published in the Southeast Asian Journal of Tropical Medicine and Public Health in 2004, volume 35, issue 2, pages 375–383. 8. Zelner JL et al. examined the protective effects of Bacillus Calmette-Guérin vaccination and isoniazid preventive therapy on contacts of tuberculosis patients. The study was published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2014, volume 189, issue 7, pages 853–859. 9. The Tuberculosis Research Centre of the Indian Council of Medical Research assessed the risk of tuberculosis among contacts of isoniazid-resistant and isoniazid-susceptible cases. The findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2011, volume 15, issue 6, pages 782–788. 10. Radhakrishna S et al. conducted a 15-year study on the additional risk of developing tuberculosis for household members with a tuberculosis case at home. The results were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2007, volume 11, issue 3, pages 282–288. 11. Narain R et al. studied the distribution of tuberculosis infection and disease among households in a rural community. The findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 1966, volume 34, issue 4, pages 639–654. 12. The WHO Tuberculosis Chemotherapy Centre investigated household contacts of open cases of pulmonary tuberculosis among the Kikuyu in Kiambu, Kenya. The study was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 1961, volume 25, issue 6, pages 831–850. 13. Andrews RH et al. examined the prevalence of tuberculosis among close family contacts of tuberculosis patients in South India and the influence of patient segregation on early attack rates. The findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 1960, volume 23, pages 463–510. 14. Loudon RG et al. analyzed 3,485 tuberculosis contacts in Edinburgh during 1954–1955. The study was published in the American Review of Tuberculosis in 1958, volume 77, issue 4, pages 623–643. 15. Triasih R et al. assessed the risk of infection and disease with Mycobacterium tuberculosis among children identified through prospective community-based contact screening in Indonesia. The study was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2015, volume 20, issue 6, pages 737–743. 16. Whalen CC et al. reported on the secondary attack rate of tuberculosis in urban households in Kampala, Uganda. The findings were published in PLoS One in 2011, volume 6, issue 2, article e16137. 17. Lewinsohn DA et al. studied whole blood interferon-gamma responses to Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens in young household contacts of tuberculosis patients in Uganda. The study was published in PLoS One in 2008, volume 3, issue 10, article e3407. 18. Amanullah F et al. reported a high prevalence of tuberculosis in children exposed at home to drug-resistant tuberculosis. The findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2014, volume 18, issue 5, pages 520–527. 19. Ma N et al. described the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of individuals resistant to Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection in a longitudinal household contact study in Kampala, Uganda. The study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2014, volume 14, article 352. 20. Rathi SK et al. investigated the prevalence and risk factors associated with tuberculin skin test positivity among household contacts of smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis cases in Umerkot, Pakistan. The findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2002, volume 6, issue 10, pages 851–857.
